name: Tone Wipe
summary: A phone photo editor whose divider you drag across the picture to compare before and after
about: A phone photo editor for a drawn lake at sunset, with the edited copy laid over the original and clipped by a divider you drag with your finger. The divider springs, clicks into place at 0, 50 and 100 percent, and the looks are real colour filters that wipe across the photo behind a warm light leak. Live sliders, a hold-to-peek at the original and a save that flies the photo into your recent edits make every step feel physical.
how: Drag the round handle, or anywhere on the photo, to slide between the original on the left and your edit on the right; it clicks at 0, 50 and 100.
Tap a look in the strip to wipe it across the picture; open Adjust to change Light, Warmth and Pop live.
Press and hold the photo, or the eye button, to peek at the untouched original.
Save flashes and flies the photo into Recent; tap a recent edit to use that look again, or Reset to start over.
Keyboard: focus the handle and use the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End; the tabs switch with the arrow keys.
